job: See the artifact before downloading it, and hand a professional ONE package that carries everything they need plus the hash that proves what it describes.
context: The exporters exist (drawings SVG, DXF, IFC4, ifcJSON, glTF/OBJ, the canonical .aura.json) and each already states its own limits honestly. What is missing is (a) a preview before commitment and (b) a single package a person can hand to a designer, engineer or builder without assembling it themselves. lib/builder/exportSource.ts resolves what an export is drawn from and already carries the canonical hash.
writeSet: app/components/builder/ExportPanel.tsx (or the existing export workspace component - find it first)
rejectionGates: the preview and the downloaded file must be the SAME BYTES - generate once, show and save the same artifact, never render a preview from a second code path
the package's stated hash must equal hashBuilderDocument of the document it was built from; a package whose hash does not match its contents must be impossible to produce
no exporter may claim graph fidelity it does not have - keep the existing per-exporter labels exactly
instructions: 1. lib/builder/handoffPackage.ts: assemble { project JSON, drawing set, cost snapshot, evidence notes, README } into one zip-less bundle (a single JSON with embedded artifacts is acceptable and keeps it dependency-free - decide and say why). It carries the canonical design hash, the budget hash, the date, and the honest limitations block verbatim.

2. Live previews: the drawing sheets already render as SVG - show them. For DXF/IFC/glTF show a real summary generated FROM the produced bytes (entity counts, sheet list, geometry mode), never a hand-written description of what it should contain.
3. Round-trip: re-importing the package must reproduce the same document hash. Pin it.
4. One button, one package, and a plain sentence about what a professional will still need to do.

verify.note: round-trip and byte-identity are the load-bearing assertions
